bc_olesen_creek_wall.blurb: Olesen Creek Wall is a cliff tucked behind the Stawamus Chief, near the Chief campground in Squamish. It holds eight trad routes, split between shorter cragging lines and a four-pitch crack-and-slab multipitch. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.11, with most at 5.10. The rock is steep in places, with a clean headwall and blocky dihedrals, and the base sits in forest. Trees shade the lower section and the wall stays out of the sun for much of a summer day, so it is a candidate when other crags are hot. Moss and lichen can cover some lines, so expect to scrub starts.

bc_cirque_of_the_uncrackables.blurb: The Cirque of the Uncrackables is a forested hollow behind the Stawamus Chief in Squamish, devoted to trad crack climbing. It has eight trad routes, and it offers more offwidth cragging than anywhere else in Squamish. A large slab sits beside long, difficult cracks, and a few hard thin cracks are here too. Grades start at 5.9, with a couple of routes each at 5.10 and 5.11, then a pair of very hard lines at 5.13 and 5.14. Sun filters through the trees from morning into mid-afternoon.

bc_the_prow_wall.blurb: The Prow Wall is a high wall on the upper Stawamus Chief in Squamish, facing the Squamish Buttress across South Gully. It holds eight trad routes, and all of it is demanding: grades run from 5.10 to 5.14, with most at 5.12 and 5.13. The climbing is multi-pitch, and the main line goes up eight pitches for roughly 200 m. On that line, the lower pitches are crack climbing that takes gear, while the upper pitches are mostly bolted.

bc_upper_south_apron.blurb: Upper South Apron is a short, clean slab just above Broadway Ledge, at the top of the South Apron on the Stawamus Chief in Squamish. Of its eight routes, seven are trad and one is sport, with grades from 5.6 to 5.10 and 5.10 the most common. Most climbers treat these lines as approach pitches on the way to the Squamish Buttress rather than as a destination of their own. Getting here means climbing up through the lower Apron, or walking the descent trail and scrambling onto the ledge.
